title: Continuation sharing for within-state action-value differences
setting: Each seed draws 4 random tabular episodic MDPs (horizon 6, 3 actions, time-layered states, sparse rewards) and samples G uniform-policy rollouts per task. Action values per (task, step, state, action) are estimated either from each visit's own sampled return (GiGPO-style) or by ConCal's recursive calibration, which matches visits by incoming state-action-state transition and blends pooled and own estimates. The metric is the error of estimated within-state pairwise action-value differences against exact values from backward dynamic programming.

paper.title: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper.claim: Pooling continuation evidence across matched visits (ConCal) gives lower error in within-group action-value differences than single-sampled-continuation estimates, without extra rollouts.

metric.name: diff_mae
metric.description: Mean absolute error between estimated and exact pairwise action-value differences Q(s,a1)-Q(s,a2), over all (task, step, state) groups where both actions were observed in the batch. Diagnostics: kendall_tau (mean sign agreement of action orderings), n_pairs, mean_pool_size (average number of visits sharing an incoming transition).

factors.name: method
factors.description: gigpo: each action value is the visit's own sampled discounted return, averaged over visits of the same (state, action). concal: recursive calibration with blend weight n/(n+1) between pooled and own transition estimate. pooled: fully pooled variant (weight 1, no retention of own estimate).

factors.name: states_per_step
factors.description: Number of states per time layer; fewer states means more revisits and larger sharing pools (near-tree at 24, dense at 3).

factors.name: noise
factors.description: Probability that a transition jumps to a uniformly random state instead of the action's nominal successor.

factors.name: group_size
factors.description: Number of rollouts G per task in the batch.
